title: Renewal-Focused QBR Facilitation Playbook (Draft)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This working draft is a facilitation playbook for QBRs where renewal outcomes are a primary goal (renew, expand, or identify risk). Intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs) running executive or platform QBRs with mid-market and enterprise accounts. Use this as a living script + checklist — shorten or expand per account maturity.

Quick guidance (top-level):
- Objective: Align on value delivered, confirm roadmap alignment, surface blockers, and secure a light-commitment toward renewal conversation (timeline, decision owner).
- Tone: consultative + executive; factual on metrics, pragmatic on risks, and explicit on asks.
- Duration: 45–60 minutes typical. For executive QBRs with multiple stakeholders consider 60 minutes.
- Required prep: renewal health snapshot, usage & cost trends, 1–2 win stories, open support items, proposed renewal ask.

Suggested agenda (45 min template):
1) 0:00–0:05 — Welcome / goals (Facilitator)
   - Script: "Thanks for joining — today we’ll align on value since last check-in, review performance & roadmap fit, and agree next steps ahead of the renewal window. We’ll keep this tight and prioritize any blockers."
2) 0:05–0:15 — Success highlights + outcomes (Customer owner + CSM)
   - Ask customer owner: "What one metric/outcome matters most to you this quarter?"
   - Present 2–3 measurable outcomes (uptime, latency, adoption, revenue attributed).
3) 0:15–0:25 — Platform health & usage trends (CSM)
   - Show Redwood Console metrics: token consumption, avg latency (p50/p95), error rate trends, embedding units used, and cost anomalies.
   - Callout: any recent incidents or config changes and remediation completed.
   - Script: "Overall service health is X — this maps to Y business impact for your team because..."
4) 0:25–0:35 — Roadmap & opportunities (Product liaison / CSM)
   - Discuss upcoming features relevant to customer (private deployment features, dedicated capacity options, Optimize recommendations).
   - Probe: confirm priority use-cases for next 6–12 months.
5) 0:35–0:45 — Risks, blockers, and renewal mechanics (CSM)
   - Surface open tickets, SLO gaps, cost concerns, or integration blockers.
   - Renewal ask framework: timeline, proposed SKU/commit level, and decision owner.
   - Script: "Based on current consumption, we recommend [option A/B]. Which of these aligns with your procurement timeline?"
6) 0:45–0:50 — Commitments & next steps (Facilitator)
   - Confirm owners and deadlines. Propose a follow-up with procurement/legal if needed.

Optional extension for 60-min exec QBR: 0:50–1:00 deep-dive on ROI and references (customer champions).

Facilitation playbook (detailed script fragments to adapt):
- Opening (build intent): "We want to make sure Redwood is continuing to deliver the outcomes you expect. Please call out any items I should prioritize in the middle of the meeting."
- If discussion goes off-rail: "This is great context — can we capture the detail and schedule 30 minutes right after to go deep so we preserve exec time?"
- When customer raises a pricing objection: "I hear cost sensitivity — can we map the cost to specific outcomes we can quantify? That will help us tailor a proposal (commit level, reserved throughput, or optimized quantization)."
- When the renewal sponsor is not present: "Can we identify the decision owner and confirm a single date window when they can review? We’ll follow up with a concise one-pager tailored to their concerns."

Pre-meeting checklist (CSM must complete 3 business days before QBR):
- [ ] Renewal window confirmed in CRM and calendar invite sent to decision owners.
- [ ] Renewal health snapshot exported (CSV/PDF): usage, cost, latency, error rate, top-3 routes by volume.
- [ ] 1–2 success stories (customer quotes, metrics) prepared as bullets/slides.
- [ ] Open support/ticket list curated with statuses and expected ETA.
- [ ] Recommended renewal options (3-tier: conservative, growth, premium) with cost delta and rationale.
- [ ] Internal sync with AE / Solutions Engineer scheduled to align on pricing and technical feasibility.
- [ ] Slide deck + one-pager created and shared 24 hours before meeting.

Attachments to prepare (templates):
- Renewal one-pager: 1 page, includes: current ARR, current commit, avg monthly usage, recommended commit, expected discount, key wins, and blockers.
- Health snapshot (2–3 slides): visuals from Redwood Console (p50/p95 latency, token trend chart, cost per token trend).
- Action tracker: simple table (owner, action, due date, status).

Renewal conversation framing (recommended language):
- Early stage (no big adoption): "We’re excited by the potential here — a small reserved commit will give you cost predictability while we scale usage."
- Growth stage (steady usage): "Your current pattern suggests option B (6–12 month reserve) gives the best unit economics while preserving burst capacity."
- Risk stage (declining usage or recurring incidents): "To protect your timelines and ensure product SLAs, let’s align on a short remediation plan + a renewal that includes a dedicated capacity pilot."

Playbook: disagreement/resolution flow
- If technical blocker unresolved: escalate to Solutions Engineering and schedule a triage (within 48 hours). Note risk to renewal in CRM.
- If procurement delay: offer a short-term extension with a bridge discount and require a decision owner and deadline.
- If cost objection persists: run a quick Optimize audit (quantization + batching) and present savings options within 5 business days.

Post-QBR follow-up template (send within 24 hours):
Subject: "QBR recap + agreed next steps — {{customer_name}}"
Body bullets:
- Key outcomes / metrics reviewed (3 bullets)
- Decisions made (renewal option chosen or next steps toward decision)
- Open actions (table inline with owners/dates)
- Next meeting: proposed date/owner
- Point of contact for procurement and technical follow-up

Scoring rubric for renewal health (quick internal use):
- Green: usage trend up or stable, <2 P1s last 90 days, executive sponsor engaged — Recommended: proactive renewal (offer: 12mo commit).
- Yellow: flat or declining usage, 2–4 P1s or major ticket backlog, sponsor engaged sporadically — Recommended: targeted remediation + renewal with shorter term.
- Red: declining usage >10%, repeated stability issues, no executive sponsor — Recommended: remediation plan + retention play and pause automated renewal until fixes confirmed.

Notes / TODOs for this doc (work-in-progress):
- Add example slide images from Redwood Console exports. (Marco to export sample charts).
- Create a 1-page procurement cheat-sheet for our Legal/Procurement common asks. (Sana to draft).
- Add language for Private deployment RFP checklist and sample contract terms (linked to legal).

Unresolved questions (for PD sync):
- Can we standardize a 30-day pilot addendum for dedicated capacity on renewal extensions? (need legal input)
- What guardrails must we include when proposing quantization as a cost-saving measure? (Research/Applied ML input)

Version notes:
